bio: William Strode (1601–1645) was an English poet and clergyman, Public Orator of Oxford University and Canon of Christ Church. His verse circulated in manuscript and was first collected long after his death.

The poem here is the one printed under his name in Frederick Locker's Lyra Elegantiarum (London: E. Moxon, 1867), an anthology of vers de société and vers d'occasion by deceased authors; the texts follow that first edition.

poems.title: Chloris in the Snow
poems.author: William Strode
poems.collection: The Oxford Book of English Verse, 1250-1900, ed. A. T. Quiller-Couch (Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1900)
poems.text:
I saw fair Chloris walk alone,
When feather’d rain came softly down,
As Jove descending from his Tower
To court her in a silver shower:
The wanton snow flew to her breast,
Like pretty birds into their nest,
But, overcome with whiteness there,
For grief it thaw’d into a tear:
  Thence falling on her garments’ hem,
  To deck her, froze into a gem.
